name: Shell Sort
description: Generalization of insertion sort that allows swapping of elements far apart. Reduces inversion count quickly by sorting elements separated by a gap, then reducing the gap.
aim: Sort by first comparing and sorting elements that are gap positions apart (starting with a large gap), then halving the gap repeatedly until gap=1 (regular insertion sort).
howItWorks: Choose initial gap (n/2 for Shell's original; Knuth: 1,4,13,40…)
Apply insertion sort on elements separated by gap
Reduce gap by dividing by 2 (or next Knuth value)
Final gap=1 pass finishes sorting with very few inversions remaining

time.bestCase: Depends on gap sequence — Knuth sequence gives O(n^{3/2})
time.averageCase: Gap sequences like Knuth's give practical O(n^1.5)
time.worstCase: Original Shell sequence; better sequences improve this

realWorld: Unix sort command historically used Shell Sort
Embedded systems where complex algorithms are hard to implement
Sorting small to medium arrays where simplicity and good performance are both needed
whenToUse: When insertion sort would be used but slightly better performance is needed
In-place sort required without recursion overhead
alternatives: Insertion Sort — simpler, better for already-sorted data
Quick Sort — better average case for large data
Merge Sort — guaranteed O(n log n) stable sort
